subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status be resolved from live gateway runtime health, from a passive local plugin status contract, or is the current `not checked` mitigation sufficient for this issue?
rationale: Current main avoids the original misleading word in `status --deep` but does not implement the requested live-runtime health source, and the remaining fix shape affects plugin/runtime ownership boundaries.

options.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require external-memory live proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove `status --deep` plus JSON status against a real external memory plugin without local plugin side effects.

options.title: Accept current mitigation
options.body: Explicitly decide that `not checked` is sufficient for normal/deep status, then close the conflicting fork PR and this issue with that product rationale.

recommendation.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
recommendation.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require external-memory live proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the current status/gateway doctor contract, and vincentkoc has recent history across the affected status, gateway, and memory-runtime files.
